biography:
Taz Douglas, a name synonymous with calculated risk and relentless pursuit in the Australian racing scene, hails from the dusty outback town of Broken Hill. His journey began not on asphalt, but on dirt, tearing around his family's sheep farm in a souped-up utility vehicle. At age 16, he entered his first local dirt track race, using the same vehicle, and placed second, narrowly missing first after being nudged off the course in the final lap. This taste of victory ignited a fire, and Taz worked tirelessly, saving every penny to eventually move into karting, then Formula Ford, and finally, the V8 Supercars series.

While he never achieved the championship glory some predicted, Taz carved out a reputation as a tenacious competitor, a driver who could extract the maximum from his equipment and capitalize on others' mistakes. His time with Team eXtreme has been a mixed bag – flashes of brilliance overshadowed by mechanical gremlins and strategic missteps. A defining moment came at Bathurst in 2018, where he dragged a severely damaged car into the top ten, showcasing his incredible resilience. 

Now, at 38, Taz is a veteran presence in the paddock. Many younger drivers have come and gone, but Taz remains, his experience and gritty determination keeping him in the game. He is currently mentoring young drivers at Team eXtreme, passing on his hard-won knowledge of the sport. While championship dreams may be fading, his passion for racing remains as fierce as ever.
drivingStyle: Taz is a master of consistency and tire management. He rarely over-drives the car, preferring to maintain a steady pace and conserve his tires for a late-race push. He is known for his ability to read the track and adapt to changing conditions, often finding grip where others struggle. Some say he is too cautious, but his calculated approach has often yielded unexpected results, particularly in endurance races where reliability and tire conservation are paramount. He is exceptional at defending his position and frustrating overtaking attempts.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry dating back to their Formula Ford days. Bellini, known for his aggressive style, often clashed with Taz's more measured approach. There was an incident at Phillip Island in 2010 where Bellini punted Taz off the track while battling for the lead.

A more recent rivalry stemming from on-track incidents during the 2021 Supercars season. Petrova accused Taz of blocking her unfairly during a race at Sandown, leading to heated exchanges in the media.
Tanaka, a relative newcomer, often beats Douglas due to having a faster car. Douglas has publicly stated, 'Give me the same car and I'll show him what real racing is.'

quirks: Always wears the same lucky pair of socks – threadbare and faded, but irreplaceable.
Listens to a specific playlist of classic rock songs before every race to calm his nerves.
Has a habit of meticulously cleaning his visor before each session, regardless of how clean it already is.
famousQuote: Racing isn't about going fast, it's about going fastest for the longest.
careerHighlight: Winning the 2015 Gold Coast 600 with a last-lap overtake, securing his only major race victory.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead at Bathurst in 2017 due to a mechanical failure with only 10 laps remaining, denying him a potentially career-defining win.
